questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests cross‑platform native bridges, queues, and lifecycle handling in React Native. It mirrors real apps needing non‑intrusive, controlled in‑app notices.

## Key Concepts
- Native module bridging (Swift/Kotlin)
- Single‑producer, single‑consumer queue
- Lifecycle: keep banners alive during navigation, cancel on unmount
- Rotation handling and memory bounds

## Code Example
```javascript
import { BannerQueue } from 'react-native'

// Enqueue a banner
BannerQueue.showBanner({
  id: 'tip1',
  title: 'Network',
  message: 'Connecting…',
  duration: 3000
})

// Dismiss explicitly
BannerQueue.dismissBanner('tip1')
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this across platforms with varying thread priorities?
- How would you extend to allow per-banner actions (tap to open)?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a robust cross-platform native module around on-device ML with real-time streaming, focusing on performance, memory safety, and privacy.

## Key Concepts

- Cross-platform native module (TurboModule/JSI)
- On-device TF Lite integration and dynamic model swapping
- Real-time streaming (20-30 Hz) with bounded queues
- Backpressure management and thread separation
- Privacy: on-device processing, minimal logging, and secure data paths

## Code Example

```javascript
// Usage sketch
const recognizer = new NativeObjectRecognizerModule();
recognizer.startStream("models/food.tflite", {fps: 25, maxDetections: 50});
recognizer.onDetection((d) => console.log(d));
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle model swaps mid-stream without dropping frames?
- How would you measure and constrain memory usage across both platforms?
